record.title: Gao–Thangadurai's zero-sum subsequence conjecture for rank-two cyclic groups
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $g(G)$ denote the smallest positive integer $t$ such that every subset $X$ of a finite abelian group $G$ with $|X|\geq t$ contains a subset $S$ with $|S|=\operatorname{exp}(G)$ and $\sum_{s\in S}s=0_G$. **Gao–Thangadurai's conjecture.** For the group $\mathbb{Z}_n^2$, one has

$$
g(\mathbb{Z}_n^2)=\begin{cases} 2n-1 & \text{if $n$ is odd},\\ 2n+1 & \text{if $n$ is even.} \end{cases}
$$

The lower bounds arise from explicit subsets of $\mathbb{Z}_n^2$ containing no zero-sum subset of cardinality $n$. The conjecture is known in several cases, including odd primes in the cited work and $n=4$; the paper proves the case $n=6$ and gives further results for even $n$.
record.source_name: Srilakshmi Krishnamoorthy, Karthikesh and Umesh Shankar, “On zero-sum subsequences of length exp(G)”, arXiv:2005.12042 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.12042

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

record.title: Homogeneous necklace matching conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mu^{\mathrm{hom}}(N)$ be the maximum number of covered beads in the worst balanced necklace under the homogeneous matching model, and define

$$
\mu^{\mathrm{hom}}=\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{\mu^{\mathrm{hom}}(N)}{N}.
$$

**Homogeneous necklace matching conjecture.**

$$
\mu^{\mathrm{hom}}=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

The conjecture concerns the homogeneous model, in which the corresponding subsequence formulation uses palindromic rather than antipalindromic subsequences. The supplied text gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Endre Csóka, Zoltán L. Blázsik, Zoltán Király and Dániel Lenger, “Upper bounds for the necklace folding problems”, arXiv:2005.12603 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.12603

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of May 2020).

record.title: The conjecture that all tie knots are alternating 2-bridge knots
record.statement:
A **tie knot** is a knot that can be represented by a tie diagram, as defined in the paper. A knot is **alternating** if it has an alternating diagram, and its **bridge number** is the minimum number of bridges among all diagrams of the knot, where a bridge is an arc containing at least one overcrossing.

**Tie-knot conjecture.** All tie knots are alternating 2-bridge knots.

The conjecture is motivated by the knot table through eight crossings: the knots absent from the tie knots are exactly the 3-bridge knots in that range, while the other listed tie knots are 2-bridge knots. The claim remains open according to the source.
record.source_name: Elizabeth Denne, Corinne Joireman and Allison Young, “The Mathematics of Tie Knots”, arXiv:2005.13000 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.13000

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2020). “We end with another open question about tie knots.”

record.title: Carlson's depth equality conjecture for finite p-groups
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite $p$-group. Define $\omega_a(G)$ as the minimum of $\dim \operatorname{H}^{*}(G;\mathbb{F}_p)/\mathfrak{p}$ over associated primes $\mathfrak{p}$ of $\operatorname{H}^{*}(G;\mathbb{F}_p)$, and let $\omega_d(G)$ be the maximum $s\geq 1$ such that $\operatorname{H}^{*}(G;\mathbb{F}_p)$ is detected by the centralizers of elementary abelian subgroups of rank $s$. **Carlson's conjecture.** Then

$$
\operatorname{depth}\operatorname{H}^{*}(G;\mathbb{F}_p)=\omega_a(G)=\omega_d(G).
$$

The preceding inequalities are known, and Carlson conjectured that both are equalities; the supplied text does not state whether the conjecture has been resolved.
record.source_name: Oihana Garaialde Ocaña, Lander Guerrero Sánchez and Jon González-Sánchez, “A family of finite p-groups satisfying Carlson's conjecture”, arXiv:2005.14452 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2002–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:math/0206127](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0206127).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14452

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

record.title: Keevash–Mubayi–Sudakov–Verstraëte rainbow Turán conjecture for even cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_{2k}$ denote the cycle of length $2k$, and let $\mathrm{ex}^*(n,H)$ be the maximum number of edges in a properly edge-coloured $n$-vertex graph containing no rainbow copy of $H$. **Keevash–Mubayi–Sudakov–Verstraëte's conjecture.** For any integer $k\geq 2$, 
$$
\mathrm{ex}^*(n,C_{2k})=\Theta(n^{1+1/k}).
$$
 This conjecture asserts that the known lower bound has the correct order of magnitude for rainbow even-cycle Turán numbers; the supplied text gives no resolution beyond the lower bound.
record.source_name: Oliver Janzer, “Rainbow Turán number of even cycles, repeated patterns and blow-ups of cycles”, arXiv:2006.01062 (2021).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1609.08212](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.08212).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.01062

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2020). “To see that this is false, note that the graph $C_{2k}[r]$ has minimum degree $2r$, but, by Theorem , for any $\d>0$, we have $\ex(n,C_{2k}[r])=O(n^{2-\frac{1}{r}+\d})$ for sufficiently large $k$.”

record.title: The one-half Minimizer-start Enclaveless Game Conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$, and let $\delta(G)$ denote its minimum degree. In the Minimizer-start competition-enclaveless game, Minimizer starts, and $\Psi_g^-(G)$ is the number of vertices chosen when both players use optimal strategies. **The one-half Minimizer-start Enclaveless Game Conjecture.**

$$
\delta(G) \ge 2 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \Psi_g^-(G) \ge \frac{1}{2}n.
$$

This conjecture gives a corresponding lower bound for the Minimizer-start version of the competition-enclaveless game. The source presents it as one of the main unsettled questions motivating the paper.
record.source_name: Michael A. Henning and Douglas F. Rall, “The Enclaveless Competition Game”, arXiv:2006.02829 (2020).

record.title: Heilbronn's triangle conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{D}$ be any convex shape in the plane, and let $\Delta(S)$ denote the minimal area of a triangle induced by a set $S$ of $s$ points in $\mathcal{D}$. Let $\Delta(s)$ be the supremum of $\Delta(S)$ over such sets. **Heilbronn's triangle conjecture.** The minimal area of the triangle induced by $s$ points in $\mathcal{D}$ satisfies

$$
\Delta(s)=O\bigg(\frac{1}{s^2}\bigg).
$$

This is the classical Heilbronn triangle problem, concerning the smallest triangle determined by points in a convex planar region. The source provides no resolution status for this conjecture.
record.source_name: Theophilus Agama, “New bounds for the Heilbronn triangle problem”, arXiv:2006.05269 (2026).

record.title: Maximum-action conjecture for triangle and square lattice graphs
record.statement: Let a triangle or square lattice graph be equipped with edge lengths, and consider the action obtained by summing the Ollivier-Ricci curvatures over its edges. The **maximum-action conjecture** states that the constant edge-length setting gives the maximum action. The paper notes that direct computation gives action zero for the constant edge-length setting; whether this setting is globally maximal is left as a conjecture.

record.title: Perfect-matching minimum-action conjecture for complete graphs
record.statement: Let $K_n$ be a complete graph with an even number of vertices, and let the action be the sum of the edge curvatures. A **perfect-matching minimum-action conjecture** states that the minimum action for $K_n$ is achieved by the perfect-matching setting, in which the action is $n$, the number of vertices. This is proposed in analogy with the tree case, while the preceding theorem establishes the maximum action for the constant edge-length setting.
record.source_name: An Huang, Bogdan Stoica, Xuyang Xia and Xiao Zhong, “Bounds on the Ricci curvature and solutions to the Einstein equations for weighted graphs”, arXiv:2006.06716 (2020).

record.title: Monotonicity of maximum likelihood degree under facial submatrices
record.statement: Let $A \in \mathbb{Z}^{n \times r}$ and $\overline{A} \in \mathbb{Z}^{n \times s}$ be a facial submatrix of $A$. The **facial-submatrix maximum likelihood degree conjecture.** The maximum likelihood degree of $\mathcal{M}_A$ is greater than or equal to the maximum likelihood degree of $\mathcal{M}_{\overline{A}}$. This would extend the preceding theorem on maximum likelihood estimators for facial subsets and express monotonicity of maximum likelihood degree under passage to a facial submatrix; the source does not provide a proof or resolution.

record.title: Conjecture on the weight distribution of a binary linear code from a two-to-one polynomial
record.statement:
Let $n=2m+1$ and let

$$
f(x)=x^{3\cdot 2^{m+1}}+x^{2^{m+2}+1}+x^{2^{m+1}+1}+x.
$$

Suppose that $f$ is considered over ${\mathbb F}_{2^n}$, and let $\mathcal{C}_{D(f)}$ denote the associated linear code. When $m\geq 4$, the conjectured parameters and possible codeword weights are

**The weight-distribution conjecture.** The polynomial $f(x)$ is two-to-one over ${\mathbb F}_{2^n}$, the code $\mathcal{C}_{D(f)}$ has parameters

$$
\left[2^{n-1}-1,n,2^{n-1}-2^{\frac{n-1}{2}}\right],
$$

and its codeword weights satisfy

$$
\mathrm{wt}(\mathbf{c}_b)\in\left\{2^{n-2},0,2^{n-2}-2^{\frac{n-3}{2}},2^{n-2}+2^{\frac{n-3}{2}},2^{n-2}-2^{\frac{n-1}{2}},2^{n-2}+2^{\frac{n-1}{2}}\right\}.
$$

The remaining problem is to determine the weight distribution of $\mathcal{C}_{D(f)}$.
record.source_name: Kangquan Li, Chunlei Li, Tor Helleseth and Longjiang Qu, “Binary linear codes with few weights from two-to-one functions”, arXiv:2006.12395 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.12395

record.title: Conjecture on the homotopical depth of higher matching complexes
record.statement: Let $M_{n-2}(K_n)$ be the matching complex of $(n-2)$-element matchings in the complete graph $K_n$, and let $M_{n-1}(K_{n,n})$ be the matching complex of $(n-1)$-element matchings in the complete bipartite graph $K_{n,n}$. The **homotopical depth conjecture.** The homotopical depth of $M_{n-2}(K_n)$ and $M_{n-1}(K_{n,n})$ is equal to the respective shifted connectivity degree. This extends known results on the homotopical depth of matching complexes and would determine these invariants for two higher matching complexes; the conjecture is presented as strongly believed in the source, with no resolution established here.

record.title: The logarithm-free extremal-number bound for split graphs
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph, let ${\rm ex}(nk,H)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $H$-free graph on $nk$ vertices, and let $f(n,H)$ denote the smallest integer $k$ for which there is an $H$-free split of $K_n$ with parts of size at most $k$. **Logarithm-free extremal-number conjecture.** There exists a positive constant $c$ such that if

$$
{\rm ex}(nk,H)>cn^2,
$$

then

$$
f(n,H)\leq k.
$$

The conjecture would remove the logarithmic factor from the paper's bound relating $f(n,H)$ to the extremal number of $H$; the supplied text gives no resolution, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Maria Axenovich and Ryan R. Martin, “Splits with forbidden subgraphs”, arXiv:2006.14466 (2025).

record.title: Regularity-free simple elevation theorem for covers
record.statement: Let $S$ be a surface and let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be covers of $S$. A closed curve on $S$ has a **simple elevation** to a cover if one of its elevations is a simple closed curve. **Regularity-free simple elevation conjecture.** Theorem on simple elevations for regular covers holds without the assumption that the covers are regular. This conjecture would address the first step in generalizing the analysis of Sunada covers: if two covers are not equivalent, one should be able to find a closed curve on the base with different simple-elevation behavior in the two covers. The result is open in the source, and its precise content depends on the omitted statement of Theorem thm:regular.

record.title: Hu–Li conjecture on the upper bound for $f(p)$
record.statement:
Let $p\ge 5$ be a prime, and let $f(p)$ be the smallest number such that every planar graph of girth $p$ with no cycles of lengths from $p+1$ through $f(p)$ admits a homomorphism to the cycle $C_p$. The **Hu–Li conjecture.**

$$
f(p)\le p(p-2).
$$

Equivalently, every planar graph of girth $p$ without cycles of lengths from $p+1$ to $p(p-2)$ is $C_p$-colorable. The paper proves finite lower and upper bounds for $f(p)$ but does not establish this proposed upper bound; it would imply Jaeger's conjecture that every planar graph of girth $2p-2$ has a homomorphism to $C_p$.
record.source_name: Xiaolan Hu and Jiaao Li, “Circular Coloring and Fractional Coloring in Planar Graphs”, arXiv:2007.00182 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2007.00182

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2020). “Conjecture remains open for each $t\ge 3$.”

record.title: The minimal-degree conjecture for triquadratic fields
record.statement:
Let $L = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{A}, \sqrt{B}, \sqrt{C})$ for distinct square-free non-zero integers $A$, $B$, and $C$, and let $M = \mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{A}, \sqrt{B})$. Here $\min\deg_L(v)$ denotes the minimum degree over $L$ among primitive-element representations of $v$ as considered in the paper. **Minimal-degree conjecture.** There exists a rational number $a$ such that

$$
\min\deg_L(\sqrt{A} + a\sqrt{B}) > [L:M].
$$

This conjecture asserts the existence of an element in every triquadratic field whose minimal degree differs from the corresponding field-extension degree. The preceding examples and results establish instances of the phenomenon, but the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Cheol-Min Park and Sun Woo Park, “Minimal Degrees of Algebraic Numbers with respect to Primitive Elements”, arXiv:2007.00956 (2021).

record.title: The bounded-dimensional large-spectrum subset conjecture over finite vector spaces
record.statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb{F}_2^n$ have density $\alpha=|A|/2^n$, and let $\eta\in[\alpha,1]$. Define the $\eta$-large spectrum by

$$
\Delta_\eta(A)=\left\{x\in\mathbb{F}_2^n:\left|\sum_{a\in A}(-1)^{a\cdot x}\right|\geqslant\eta|A|\right\}.
$$

The dimension of a subset of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ is the size of its largest linearly independent subset.

**Bounded-dimensional spectrum conjecture.** There exists $\Delta'\subset\Delta_\eta(A)$ such that

$$
|\Delta'|\geqslant\eta^2|\Delta_\eta(A)|
$$

and

$$
\dim(\Delta')\lesssim_\alpha 1.
$$

This is the finite-vector-space restatement of the small-dimensional subset conjecture in the concrete model case. The paper presents it as an open challenge, and any proof or disproof would be significant.
record.source_name: Thomas F. Bloom and Olof Sisask, “Breaking the logarithmic barrier in Roth's theorem on arithmetic progressions”, arXiv:2007.03528 (2021).

record.title: Inverse Turán conjecture for the four-cycle
record.statement:
Let $C_4$ denote the cycle of length four, and let $\operatorname{ex}^{-1}(k,H)$ denote the inverse Turán number of $H$, namely the maximum number of edges in a graph whose every $H$-free subgraph has fewer than $k$ edges. **Inverse Turán conjecture for the four-cycle.**

$$
\operatorname{ex}^{-1}(k,C_4)=\frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3\sqrt{3}}k^{3/2}+o(k^{3/2}).
$$

The paper gives upper and lower bounds for $\operatorname{ex}^{-1}(k,C_4)$ and states that this conjectured value is asymptotically sharp for the lower bound; the conjecture remains open in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Ervin Győri, Nika Salia, Casey Tompkins and Oscar Zamora, “Inverse Turán numbers”, arXiv:2007.07042 (2021).

record.title: The extremal inequality for Kruskal–Katona functions
record.statement:
Let $n\ge 4$ be an even integer, and let $a$ and $k$ be integers satisfying

$$
0\le a,k\le {n\choose n/2}.
$$

Here, $\kappa_{n/2}$ and $\kappa^*_{n/2}$ denote the Kruskal–Katona-type functions defined in the paper. **The extremal inequality.**

$$
\kappa_{n/2}\left({n\choose n/2}\right)+\kappa_{n/2}(k)\le \kappa_{n/2}(a)+\kappa^*_{n/2}\left(k+{n\choose n/2}-a\right).
$$

This inequality would provide the tight upper bound for the maximum size of two antichains having exactly $k$ disjoint pairs, including the case where $\kappa(k)<\kappa^*(k)$. It has been verified for small even values of $n$, but a proof remains elusive.
record.source_name: Wong W. H. W. and E. G. Tay, “Kruskal-Katona's function and a variation of cross-intersecting antichains”, arXiv:2007.07094 (2020).

record.title: Frid's conjecture on bounded palindromic length sequences
record.statement:
For a finite word, its **palindromic length** is the minimum number of palindromes whose concatenation is the word. For an infinite word, its palindromic length sequence records the palindromic lengths of all its finite prefixes.

**Frid's conjecture.** The palindromic length sequence of an infinite word is bounded if and only if the infinite word is ultimately periodic.

This conjecture connects bounded palindromic complexity with eventual periodicity of infinite words. The supplied text attributes it to the cited authors but gives no evidence resolving it.
record.source_name: Shuo Li, “Palindromic length sequence of the ruler sequence and of the period-doubling sequence”, arXiv:2007.08317 (2020).

record.title: Monotonicity and convergence of discretized quartic minimization problems
record.statement: Consider the discretized problem with discretization parameter $N$, its smallest eigenvalue, and its optimal value, together with the corresponding original problem. **Monotonicity and convergence conjecture.** The smallest eigenvalue and the optimal value of the discretized problem are monotone nondecreasing with $N$ when $N$ is large enough, and converge to those of the original problem. This conjecture is motivated by numerical results for the discretized problems, which indicate increasing smallest eigenvalues and optimal values as $N$ grows; its general validity is not established in the supplied text.

record.title: Bank's hypertranscendency conjecture for perturbations of the gamma function
record.statement:
Let $h$ be an entire function, let $\Gamma$ denote the Euler gamma function, and let $\mathcal{M}_0$ be the field of meromorphic functions $y$ satisfying $T(r,y)=o(r)$ as $r\rightarrow\infty$ outside a set of finite measure. **Bank's conjecture.** The function

$$
\Gamma e^h
$$

should be hypertranscendental over $\mathcal{M}_0$, meaning that it satisfies no nontrivial algebraic differential equation with coefficients in $\mathcal{M}_0$. Bank posed this question to determine whether the hypertranscendency of $\Gamma$ is caused by the nature of its poles and zeros; the conjecture is stated here without evidence of a resolution.

record.title: Infinitesimal Torelli conjecture for elliptic surfaces with d=1
record.statement:
Let $\pi:X\to C$ be an elliptic surface, let $d=1$, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be its associated line bundle with $h^0(\mathcal{L})>0$.

**Infinitesimal Torelli conjecture.** $X$ does not satisfy infinitesimal Torelli.

The claim concerns the remaining case where the degree of the associated line bundle is one and it has a nonzero global section. The preceding discussion explains that known criteria involving the multiplication map do not by themselves determine the failure of infinitesimal Torelli in this case; the assertion is presented as a conjectural expectation.

record.title: Minimum weighted Szeged index graphs are attained by trees
record.statement: Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $wSz(G)$ denote its weighted Szeged index. **Tree attainment conjecture.** The minimum weighted Szeged index among $n$-vertex graphs is attained by a tree. This would reduce the problem of characterizing minimum weighted Szeged index graphs to the study of trees; the paper presents computational evidence and structural results for minimum weighted Szeged index trees, but does not resolve the conjecture.

record.title: Boros, Caro, Füredi and Yuster's asymptotic conjecture for non-repeated cycle lengths
record.statement:
Let $f_2(n)$ denote the maximum, over all $n$-vertex 2-connected graphs, of the number of cycle lengths that occur exactly once. The authors' conjecture is

$$
\lim_{n\to \infty} f_2(n)/\sqrt{n} =1.
$$

This conjecture asserts that the lower bound obtained from Sidon sequences is asymptotically tight. The known construction gives $f_2(n)\geq \sqrt{n}-o(\sqrt{n})$, while the matching upper bound remains open.

record.title: Italian domination conjecture for the Cartesian product of a 4-cycle and an odd cycle
record.statement:
Let $C_n$ be the cycle on an odd integer $n$, and let $C_4\square C_n$ denote their Cartesian product. For an **Italian dominating function** on a graph, assign each vertex a value in $\{0,1,2\}$ so that every vertex assigned $0$ has neighboring assigned values with sum at least $2$; let $\gamma_I$ be the minimum weight of such a function. **Italian domination conjecture.**

$$
\gamma_I(C_4\square C_n)=2n+2.
$$

The paper determines exact values for several Cartesian products of cycles, while the cases not covered by those results remain open; this conjecture addresses the case of a 4-cycle and an odd cycle.

record.title: Fujita–Magnant conjecture on properly colored Hamiltonian cycles
record.statement:
Let $(G,c)$ be an edge-colored graph on $n\geq 3$ vertices. For each vertex $v$, let $d^c_G(v)$ be the number of colors on edges incident with $v$, and let $\delta^c(G)$ be the minimum of these values over all vertices. A graph is **properly Hamiltonian** if it contains a properly colored Hamiltonian cycle. **Fujita–Magnant conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^c(G)\geq\frac{n+1}{2},
$$

then $G$ is properly Hamiltonian. The source notes that Fujita and Magnant showed the condition is sharp by constructing an example, while the conjecture itself is presented as open.
record.source_name: Xiaozheng Chen and Xueliang Li, “Proper vertex-pancyclicity of edge-colored complete graphs without joint monochromatic triangles”, arXiv:2007.14099 (2020).

record.title: Fujita–Magnant conjecture on proper vertex-pancyclicity
record.statement:
Let $(G,c)$ be an edge-colored complete graph on $n\geq 3$ vertices. For each vertex $v$, let $d^c_G(v)$ be the number of colors on edges incident with $v$, and let $\delta^c(G)$ be the minimum of these values over all vertices. The graph is **properly vertex-pancyclic** if every vertex lies on a proper cycle of every length $\ell$ with $3\leq\ell\leq n$. **Fujita–Magnant conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^c(G)\geq\frac{n+1}{2},
$$

then $G$ is properly vertex-pancyclic. This strengthens the corresponding properly Hamiltonian conjecture by requiring proper cycles of every admissible length through every vertex; the source presents it as an open conjecture.

record.title: Burr–Erdős linear Ramsey conjecture for bounded-degree graphs
record.statement: Let $\Delta\in\mathbb{N}$. A graph has **bounded maximum degree** at most $\Delta$ when $\Delta(G)\leq\Delta$. **Burr–Erdős conjecture.** There exists $c=c(\Delta)>0$ such that every $2$-edge-colored $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of every graph $G$ with at most $cn$ vertices and $\Delta(G)\leq\Delta$. This is a foundational linear Ramsey-number conjecture for sparse graphs; the supplied source does not indicate whether this formulation is resolved.

record.title: Maximal rank conjecture for varieties with a hypersurface secant variety
record.statement:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^N$ be a smooth non-degenerate projective variety, and let $g$ be the generic $X$-rank. Denote by $r_{\text{max}}$ the maximum $X$-rank and by $r_{\text{max},g-1}$ the maximum $X$-rank achieved on the secant variety $\sigma_{g-1}(X)$. Assume that $\sigma_{g-1}(X)$ is a hypersurface. **Maximal rank conjecture.**

$$
r_{\text{max}}=\max\{r_{\text{max},g-1},g\}.
$$

This conjecture refines the preceding upper bound on the maximal $X$-rank by asserting that the maximum is attained either on $\sigma_{g-1}(X)$ or at the generic rank. Its status is not resolved in the supplied source.

record.title: The maximum-length conjecture for circuit codes with long bit runs
record.statement:
Let $k$ and $l$ be integers at least $2$ of opposite parity, with $k\geq 2l+1$ if $k$ is odd and $k\geq 2l-2$ if $k$ is even, and set

$$
d=\frac{1}{2}(3k+l+1).
$$
 Here $S(d,k,k+l)$ denotes the maximum length of a circuit code with parameters $(d,k,k+l)$, and $K(d,k)$ denotes the relevant upper-bound quantity for circuit-code lengths.

**Maximum-length conjecture.** Under these conditions,

$$
S(d,k,k+l)=K(d,k).
$$

This strengthens the previously recalled conjecture for odd $k$ and even $l$, extending the predicted equality to opposite-parity pairs satisfying the stated bounds. The equality is confirmed in several cases, including $l=2$ or $4$ with odd $k$, and the result for $l=3$ with even $k$ in the cited theorems; the general assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Kevin M. Byrnes, “The Maximum Length and Isomorphism of Circuit Codes with Long Bit Runs”, arXiv:2008.04839 (2020).

record.title: Bartley–Day conjecture on cycles in tournaments
record.statement:
Let $C(n,\ell)$ be the maximum number of cycles of length $\ell$ in an $n$-vertex tournament. Let

$$
R(n,\ell)=\frac{(\ell-1)!}{2^{\ell}}\binom{n}{\ell}
$$

be the expected number of such cycles in a random $n$-vertex tournament, and define

$$
c(\ell)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{C(n,\ell)}{R(n,\ell)}.
$$

**Bartley–Day conjecture.** For $\ell\ge 3$, $c(\ell)=1$ if and only if $\ell$ is not divisible by four. The statement is known for regular tournaments and for $\ell\le 8$. The paper proves the claim for $\ell$ not divisible by four and notes that $c(\ell)>1$ when $\ell$ is divisible by four, so this conjecture is settled.
record.source_name: Andrzej Grzesik, Daniel Kral, Laszlo Miklos Lovasz and Jan Volec, “Cycles of a given length in tournaments”, arXiv:2008.06577 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.06577

record.title: Bartley–Day conjecture for cycle lengths divisible by four
record.statement:
Let $C(n,\ell)$ be the maximum number of cycles of length $\ell$ in an $n$-vertex tournament. Let

$$
R(n,\ell)=\frac{(\ell-1)!}{2^{\ell}}\binom{n}{\ell}
$$

be the expected number of such cycles in a random $n$-vertex tournament, and define

$$
c(\ell)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{C(n,\ell)}{R(n,\ell)}.
$$

**Bartley–Day conjecture.** If $\ell$ is divisible by four, then

$$
c(\ell)=1+2\cdot\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\left(\frac{2}{(2i-1)\pi}\right)^{\ell}.
$$

The paper presents this as an extension of a problem posed by Savchenko and attributes it to Day; its asymptotically tight bounds provide evidence, but no proof is given here.

record.title: Wu–Zhang–Li equitable vertex arboricity conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. A **vertex $k$-arborable** graph has a (not necessarily proper) $k$-coloring whose color classes induce acyclic subgraphs; it is **equitably vertex $k$-arborable** if the sizes of the color classes differ by at most one. Let $\Delta(G)$ denote the maximum degree.

**Wu–Zhang–Li conjecture.** Graph $G$ is equitably vertex $k$-arborable whenever

$$
k\geq \left\lceil\frac{\Delta(G)+1}{2}\right\rceil.
$$

The conjecture is a well-known equitable analogue of vertex arboricity and has received attention in the literature; the supplied text does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Hemanshu Kaul, Jeffrey A. Mudrock and Michael J. Pelsmajer, “On Equitable List Arboricity of Graphs”, arXiv:2008.08926 (2021).
record.references:

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08926

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2020). “Their conjecture is still open and is known as the Equitable $\Delta$-Coloring Conjecture.”

record.title: Improved equitable list arboricity conjecture for connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $\Delta(G)$ denote its maximum degree. The graph is **equitably $k$-list arborable** if every $k$-assignment admits an arborable list coloring in which each color class has size at most $\lceil |V(G)|/k\rceil$.

**Improved equitable list arboricity conjecture.** Any connected graph $G$ is equitably $\lceil\Delta(G)/2\rceil$-list arborable provided $G$ is neither a cycle nor a complete graph of odd order.

This conjecture seeks to improve the bound in Zhang's equitable list arboricity conjecture. Its status is not specified in the supplied text.

record.title: Sullivan's conjecture on feedback arc sets in m-free digraphs
record.statement:
Let $m\ge 3$, and let $G$ be an $m$-free digraph, meaning that $G$ has no directed cycle of length at most $m$. Let $\beta(G)$ be the minimum number of edges whose removal makes $G$ acyclic, and let $\gamma(G)$ be the number of unordered pairs of nonadjacent vertices of $G$. **Sullivan's conjecture.**

$$
\beta(G)\le \frac{2}{(m+1)(m-2)}\gamma(G).
$$

Sullivan proposed this as a best-possible general bound. The paper states related results for several values of $m$, but does not report a resolution of the general conjecture.

record.title: Fujita and Magnant's vertex-pancyclic conjecture for properly colored cycles
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an edge-colored complete graph on $n$ vertices. Write $\delta^c(G)$ for its minimum color degree, where the color degree of a vertex is the number of colors on its incident edges. A cycle is **properly colored** if consecutive edges have distinct colors.

**Fujita and Magnant's conjecture.** If

$$
\delta^c(G)\geq \frac{n+1}{2},
$$

then every vertex of $G$ is contained in properly colored cycles of every length from $3$ to $n$.

Fujita and Magnant proved the assertion for properly colored triangles and quadrangles, and later work established it for cycles of length at least the minimum color degree. The conjecture is known when the graph contains no monochromatic triangles, but is otherwise open.

record.title: Bollobás and Erdős's properly colored Hamilton cycle conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an edge-colored complete graph on $n$ vertices. Write $\Delta^{mon}(G)$ for the maximum monochromatic degree, namely the maximum, over all vertices, of the number of incident edges having one common color. A cycle is **properly colored** if consecutive edges have distinct colors, and a Hamilton cycle is one containing every vertex of $G$.

**Bollobás and Erdős's conjecture.** If

$$
\Delta^{mon}(G)<\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor,
$$

then $G$ contains a properly colored Hamilton cycle.

This is a central sufficient-condition conjecture for properly colored Hamilton cycles in edge-colored complete graphs. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved, so its status is recorded as open.

record.title: Aboulker et al.'s directed cycle subdivision conjecture
record.statement:
Let $C_\ell$ be the undirected cycle of length $\ell$, and let $C$ be an orientation of $C_\ell$. For a digraph $F$, let $\operatorname{mader}_{\vec{\chi}}(F)$ be the smallest integer $k\ge1$ such that every digraph $D$ with dichromatic number $\vec{\chi}(D)\ge k$ contains a subdivision of $F$. **Aboulker et al.'s conjecture.** If $C$ is an orientation of $C_\ell$, then

$$
\operatorname{mader}_{\vec{\chi}}(C)=\ell.
$$

This conjecture concerns the threshold at which large dichromatic number forces subdivisions of directed cycles. The paper's abstract states that this conjecture is settled by proving the asserted equality.

record.title: The linear Mader-number conjecture for Mader-perfect digraphs
record.statement:
For a positive integer $k$, let $m(k)$ denote the maximum number of arcs in a Mader-perfect digraph on $k$ vertices. A digraph is **Mader-perfect** when its dichromatic Mader number equals its number of vertices. **The linear Mader-number conjecture.**

$$
m(k)=O(k).
$$

The paper gives the upper bound $m(k)=O(k^{3/2}\sqrt{\log k})$ and the lower bound $m(k)\ge 2k-1$, so the conjecture asks whether the true order of growth is linear.
